# Psalm 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of-David. To-You, YHWH, my-soul I-lift-up.

**2** My-God, in-You I-trust; let-me-not be-put-to-shame; let-not my-enemies exult over-me.

**3** Indeed, none who-wait-for-You shall-be-put-to-shame; put-to-shame shall-be those-who-act-treacherously without-cause.

**4** Your-ways, YHWH, make-known to-me; Your-paths teach-me.

**5** Lead-me in-Your-truth and-teach-me, for You [are] the-God of-my-salvation; for-You I-wait all the-day.

**6** Remember Your-compassions, YHWH, and-Your-steadfast-love, for from-of-old [are] they.

**7** The-sins of-my-youth and-my-transgressions do-not remember; according-to-Your-steadfast-love remember-me, for-the-sake-of Your-goodness, YHWH.

**8** Good and-upright [is] YHWH; therefore He-instructs sinners in-the-way.

**9** He-guides the-humble in-justice, and-teaches the-humble His-way.

**10** All the-paths of-YHWH [are] steadfast-love and-truth, for-those-keeping His-covenant and-His-testimonies.

**11** For-Your-name's-sake, YHWH, pardon my-iniquity, for it [is] great.

**12** Who [is] the-man fearing YHWH? He-will-instruct-him in-the-way he-should-choose.

**13** His-soul shall-abide in-good, and-his-seed shall-inherit the-land.

**14** The-counsel of-YHWH [is] for-those-who-fear-Him, and-His-covenant He-makes-known to-them.

**15** My-eyes [are] continually toward YHWH, for He brings-out from-the-net my-feet.

**16** Turn to-me and-be-gracious to-me, for lonely and-afflicted [am] I.

**17** The-distresses of-my-heart have-enlarged; from-my-straits bring-me-out.

**18** See my-affliction and-my-trouble, and-forgive all my-sins.

**19** See my-enemies, for they-are-many, and-with-violent hatred they-hate-me.

**20** Guard my-soul and-deliver-me; let-me-not be-put-to-shame, for I-take-refuge in-You.

**21** Integrity and-uprightness preserve-me, for I-wait-for-You.

**22** Redeem Israel, O-God, from-all its-distresses.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **25:1**: An acrostic psalm — each verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with slight irregularities (the letter vav is missing; pe is doubled).

— EMET
